steps.text: The PR reworks eval token budgets per model family, and three surfaces render remaining tokens. If one eval's retry can shift the calculation, every surface lies at once. Let me read the diff before saying anything.
Reading the diff on **#412 — Cap eval-run token budget per model family**.

The arithmetic itself is clean — one cap table, one ledger, remaining tokens derived instead of a shared org pool. What I want to check is whether two evals can race it: `remaining` resolves from the family alone, with no run-group id in the key.

steps.text: Three independent callers, and `extensions.py` recomputes after a retry is recorded. Two evals can share one run-group id — a nightly sweep and an ad-hoc grade kicked off the same hour — so one eval's retry burns the other run's remaining tokens everywhere they render. That is the "budget moved on its own" report from last month.

I left one blocking comment on `budget.py:9` asking for the run-group id in the ledger key, and approved the rest. Remaining-tokens reads through the ledger and needs no migration — that part is correct.

**Summary:** 1 blocking comment, 3 nits, no test coverage for the shared run-group case.
